newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Coup plot general's widow leaves Morocco for France.
newsitem.headline: Coup plot general's widow leaves Morocco for France.

text.p: The widow of former Moroccan defence minister Mohamed Oufkir, who died after a failed coup against King Hassan in 1972, flew on Monday to France for a short visit after long being banned from leaving Morocco, a family member said.
"Fatima Oufkir went on Monday to France for a three-week private visit with her youngest child, Abdallah. She will be back home after that," a relative told Reuters by telephone.
"She left by Royal Air Maroc at around 9 a.m. (0900 GMT) from Casablanca. It is her first trip abroad," the relative said. Two other children remained in Morocco.
The general's widow and his family had long been banned from leaving the country after Oufkir was said to have been implicated in a coup plot against the king.
The widow went to the airport with her lawyer Mohamed Naciri.
No official comment was immediately available.
Three of General Oufkir's children were allowed to fly to France last July.

The general, a power behind the throne for years, was officially said to have committed suicide after Moroccan Air Force planes tried to shoot down the king's plane as it flew home from France in 1972. Opposition sources said he was summarily shot.
Fatima, six children and a relative were held in detention before being released in 1991 after a campaign by human rights groups. But they were banned from leaving Morocco.
